pairs.subject: connector-catalog
pairs.evidence: src/features/admin/integrations/IntegrationsPanel.tsx:99 Rather than rendering connection setup through a uniform schema-driven form derived from catalog declarations, the dashboard dispatches across hardcoded provider panels.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/integrations/providers.ts:23 Fidelity tiers ('measured', 'allocated', 'seats-only') explicitly declare connector capabilities, preventing missing spend data like Copilot's from producing fabricated zeroes in downstream views.

src/lib/integrations/providers.ts:28 ProviderDef omits auth schemas and probe recipes from the catalog row, preventing consuming surfaces from rendering uniformly and requiring per-provider component dispatch.

src/features/admin/integrations/IntegrationsPanel.tsx:101 Acquisition surfaces are hand-crafted per-provider React components (ClaudeCodeSetup, CopilotSetup, OpenAISetup) rather than a single generic form renderer driven by declared auth schemas.
src/lib/integrations/providers.ts:24 While status flags gate UI affordances, persistent catalog version stamps, tombstones, and dependent migration mechanisms do not apply to an in-code static list.
src/lib/integrations/providers.ts:26 Integration types are a closed set of fixed internal provider IDs; foreign reference resolution, alias tables, and ranking tiers are not implemented.
src/lib/integrations/providers.ts:72 Providers are defined as an immutable static in-code array with no database table or operator editing door, so two-writer refresh conflicts do not apply.

pairs.registryProposal: For static in-code catalogs with a small, fixed set of integrations, the standard should clarify whether per-provider setup dispatch is treated as an acceptable form of adapter registration or a strict deviation from catalog-as-data.
